source: Hand-curated limits on the ICAO aerodrome code (A-F) of stands whose OpenStreetMap spacing misjudges their size: the import derives a code from the distance to the nearest mapped stand, then a rule with the longest matching stand-name prefix raises it to at_least and caps it at at_most. No airport publishes a stand table openly; EDDK uses the VATSIM Germany knowledge base (unofficial, flight-simulation community: 'EDDK Ground', knowledgebase.vatsim-germany.org/books/sops-fir-langen/page/eddk-ground, read November 2026). Terminal piers A-D carry no published size there; they serve A320 and B737 jets daily, so code C is a lower bound estimated from the airlines' fleets.

rules.note: Terminal 1 (piers A-C) and Terminal 2 (pier D) contact and apron stands: estimate from the A320/B737 fleets of Eurowings, Ryanair and the leisure carriers; VATSIM names D51 as a code C stand
Cargo aprons E and F: 'most of the heavy lifting cargo fleet (e.g. B747)' (VATSIM Germany)
A380 positions, primary E31, E33, E35, E41, E45 and secondary E43, F21, F23, F25, F31 (VATSIM Germany)
Cargo feeder apron W: 'B737, ATR and B757/B767' (VATSIM Germany)
Apron V: cargo feeders up to B757/B767 and business aviation 'up to B737-BBJ' depending on the position (VATSIM Germany); the spacing decides which
